# Goban Studio v10.0.0

v10 is about the first ten minutes: a new mark, a placement quiz for
players who already know the rules, a Learn path you can read at a
glance, and a calmer Play home. v10 reads everything v9 saved.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. Windows on ARM runs the x64
build under the system's emulation.

## A new mark

Two stones on diagonal points (kosumi) on a plain board, seen from straight
above: a matte black stone and a shell white stone on a calm honey surface
with a fine grid. The app icon, the sidebar and the welcome screen now use
this one picture. The wood-grain texture that only the old icon used is
gone.

## Find your level first

If you told the app at the start that you know the rules or already play,
Learn now offers a short placement quiz before your first path: six
problems, about three minutes.

- It starts at an easy grade; each problem you solve makes the next one a
  grade harder, each one you miss a grade easier. Your first answer to
  each problem counts. A hint or the answer counts as missed.
- The result sets where the course starts (players who place at grade 3 or
  above skip the beginner units and capture Go) and which problems you get
  first, until your own results measure your level.
- *Not now* is remembered, and the path starts from what you said at the
  start.

## A path you can read

Problems in Learn's path now show their position as a small tile, so four
problems with the same title ("Capture") no longer look identical.

## A calmer Play home

The classics list starts with the four best-known games and one link to all
twenty. A classic's date now shows just its year (1846), not the SGF's list
of playing days.

## Fixes

- Two checks that depended on timing now run the same way every time: the
  Windows updater's locked-file retry, and the screenshot comparison
  (which could catch a thumbnail before it was drawn).
- `docs/plan.md` describes the v9 player model and Learn's path again.

## Known limits

- The builds are not code-signed (no certificates yet). The update
  checksum guards against damaged or wrong downloads; it is not a
  signature.
- Not yet checked by people: a usability test of the placement quiz and
  the two-space layout, a strong player's review of the course, a
  native-speaker review of the Chinese, Korean and Japanese text, and a
  real screen-reader session.
- The placement quiz has six problems, so it places roughly; the level is
  refined as you solve problems in Learn.
- *Try again* needs KataGo (the desktop app); the browser preview has no
  KataGo.
- The KataGo check of the course leaves some steps for a human (rule
  steps, small shape boards, endgame boards with open areas, one 3-3
  joseki step).
- 13×13 handicap games were not measured; the standard ladder's 10-kyu
  anchor was not measured again.
- The counting solver ignores ko threats; endgame problems avoid ko.
